**The platform draws on 78 million rows from three sources: 33.2 million from real SAP BDC (36 sources, 80 objects), 44.6 million from operational systems (11 sources for fleet telemetry and mining execution), and 445,000 stand-in rows (12 sources) where SAP APIs were unavailable.**

What stands out is the operational dominance—two-thirds of the volume comes from mining operations raw data (44.6 M rows, primarily fleet movements and sensor telemetry), while SAP provides the finance and master-data backbone (journal entries, purchase orders, invoices, workforce, equipment). The stand-in slice is small (0.6% of total rows) but covers 12 distinct sources, suggesting gaps in SAP BDC coverage that required simulation.

**Why it matters:** Finance (13.7 M journal entry rows, 4.6 M headers) and procurement (3.9 M purchase-order rows, 2.0 M invoices) anchor cost-per-tonne analysis in real transactional truth, while the OPS layer (27.6 M + 16.6 M + 0.5 M rows) tracks actual dig, haul, and crush performance. Stand-ins fill holes but require validation before decisions.

**Next step:** Audit the 12 SAP_STANDIN sources (376,973 + 60,170 rows from SAP_SIM) to prioritise which BDC APIs to onboard next, eliminating synthetic data where business impact is highest.
